history: Fromage is named after its container. Latin had a word for cheese, caseus. But Medieval Latin also said formaticus, with caseus understood: ‘cheese made in a mould’, from forma, the mould in which the cheese was shaped. In the end the adjective did all the work and the noun disappeared. Old French said formage, and the r later moved, giving fromage, already found in the Couronnement de Louis around 1135. Occitan still says formatge, and Italian formaggio has the same origin. The mould survives in French as forme and fourme, as in fourme d'Ambert, a blue cheese. Spanish queso, Italian cacio and Portuguese queijo come from the other Latin word, caseus.
historyEinfach: In Latin, cheese was caseus. But people also said formaticus: ‘made in a mould’. A mould is a form that gives the cheese its shape. In old French the word was formage. Later the letters changed places, and it became fromage. Italian formaggio comes from the same word. Spanish queso comes from caseus.

elsewhere.text: Spanish and Portuguese kept the old Latin noun, caseus. French and Italian kept the adjective that went with it, ‘made in a mould’.
